column3: MT 19:3. “The deliverance” is rendered “the victory,” and NASB adds “it said.”
MT 19:4. “Who are ashamed” is rendered “who are humiliated.”
MT 19:6. “Put to shame the faces” is rendered “covered with shame the faces,” and “rescued” as “saved.”
MT 19:7. “That not are to you commanders and servants” is rendered “princes and servants are nothing to you,” and “right in your eyes” as “you would be pleased.”
MT 19:8. “Speak to the heart of your servants” is rendered “speak kindly to your servants”; the oath form “if a man will lodge” becomes “surely not a man will pass the night.”
MT 19:18. “Rushed ahead to the Jordan” is rendered “rushed to the Jordan.”
MT 19:19. The Hebrew “the ford passed over” is rendered “they kept crossing the ford”; the meaning is uncertain.
MT 19:25. “Had not done his feet … his moustache” is rendered “neither cared for his feet, nor trimmed his mustache.”
MT 19:26. The Hebrew reads “he came to Jerusalem”; NASB has “from Jerusalem.”
MT 19:29. “Men of death” is rendered “dead men,” and “righteousness” as “right.”
MT 19:30. “Why do you still speak your words?” is rendered “Why do you still speak of your affairs?”, and “I say” as “I have decided.”
MT 19:31. Close to the Hebrew; “in peace” is rendered “safely.”
